title.narrative: WASH intervention to benefit vulnerable families and communities in the 4 most affected municipalities of Guantanamo.

description.narrative: The winds and unprecedented flooding caused by Hurricane Oscar caused great damage to homes and affected the supply of drinking water to families and public institutions in the province of Guantánamo, with the greatest damage in the municipalities of San Antonio del Sur, Imias, Baracoa and Maisi. The national authorities have defined as a priority the efforts to reestablish water supply and sanitation services in the affected communities. The project plans to support the restoration of access to drinking water, adequate conditions for its storage, distribution and treatment, as well as the improvement of basic hygiene and sanitation conditions for approximately 74,000 people. Work will be carried out at three levels: provision of safe water supply at the community level; increase water storage capacities of health and education institutions; and improve hygiene and sanitation conditions of vulnerable families. From existing stocks, UNICEF has already delivered 1,500 tanks of 10-liter and 100 tanks of 1,000-liter to improve water storage conditions in schools. In total, UNICEF will deliver 10,000 water containers (10 liter) and 240 water tanks (1,000 liter). UNICEF has also delivered 1,000 roof sheets for the rehabilitation of lost ceilings and school supplies for the immediate response, as part of the coordination between the WASH and Education sectors.
